extraction.name: FLORES-101
extraction.description: The FLORES-101 evaluation benchmark, consisting of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and covering a variety of different topics and domains. These sentences have been translated in 101 languages by professional translators through a carefully controlled process.
extraction.creator: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc’Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzmán, Angela Fan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The construction process consisted of extracting sentences from English Wikipedia, running pilot experiments to determine the translation process, and launching the actual translation workflow for over 100 languages.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Sentences were extracted from English Wikipedia, specifically Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Sentences were manually selected from random articles, avoiding very short or malformed sentences, and balanced across the beginning, middle, and end of the articles.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Source sentences were sent to translation Language Service Providers (LSPs). Translated data was edited by different translators within the LSP, passed through automated quality control, and then sent to an independent evaluation LSP for quality assessment. Failed translations were sent back for re-translation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Translation quality was assessed using a Translation Quality Score (0-100 scale) based on identified errors such as grammar, punctuation, spelling, capitalization, addition/omission of information, mistranslation, unnatural translation, untranslated text, and register.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 10 different annotators (6 male, 4 female) with roles as researchers and program/project managers, originating from East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America, and North America.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors hope to expand the number of languages and make the test set available for community efforts and shared tasks.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to foster progress in machine translation for low-resource languages, benefiting the majority of the world's population who speak these languages.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: To avoid bias from document structure, paragraphs were equally distributed from the beginning, middle, and end of articles. The authors also note the potential for translationese (literal or awkward translations) but consider its effects marginal for low-resource evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset relies on English source sentences translated into other languages, which may introduce translationese (overly literal or awkward translations).
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is divided into dev (for hyper-parameter tuning), devtest (for testing during development), and test splits. It can be used for machine translation evaluation, sentence and document classification, language identification, and multilingual domain adaptation.

inLanguage.evidence: These sentences have been translated in 101 languages by professional translators through a carefully controlled process.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: First, we extracted sentences to translate from English Wikipedia. Second, we designed and ran pilot experiments to determine the translation process, and finally we launched the actual translation workflow for over 100 languages.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: All source sentences were extracted from multiple Wikimedia sources... The sentence selection process consisted of selecting an article at random from each source, and then manually selecting a few (typically between 3 and 5) contiguous sentences from each article...

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: All source sentences were extracted from multiple Wikimedia sources... In particular, we collected a third of the sentences from Wikinews, which is a collection of international news articles, a third from Wikijunior, which is a collection of age-appropriate nonfiction books for children from birth to age 12, and a third from WikiVoyage which is a travel guide...

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: The sentence selection process consisted of selecting an article at random from each source, and then manually selecting a few (typically between 3 and 5) contiguous sentences from each article, avoiding segments with very short or malformed sentences.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: For each language, all source sentences are sent to a certain translation LSPs. Once sentences are translated, the data is sent to different translators within the LSP for editing and then moves on to automated quality control steps... Afterwards, translations are sent to an evaluation LSP that performs quality assessment... If the score is below the accepted threshold, translations together with the assessment report are sent back to the translation LSP for re-translation.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: We assess translation quality through a Translation Quality Score, calculated per language on a 0 to 100 scale. The translation quality score is determined based on the number of identified errors by the evaluation LSPs. The following errors are examined: grammar, punctuation, spelling, capitalization, addition or omission of information, mistranslation, unnatural translation, untranslated text, and register.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: The selection process was performed by 10 different annotators in our lab, 6 male and 4 female; with different roles in research: researchers (scientists and engineers) and program/project managers; originally coming from different regions of the world: East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America and North America.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: We hope to continue to expand the number of languages covered in FLORES-101 and make the test set available to various community efforts to improve translation systems in shared tasks such as those from the Workshop on Machine Translation.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Yet, the majority of the world’s population speak low-resource languages and would benefit from improvements in translation quality on their native languages... By publicly releasing such a high-quality and high-coverage dataset, we hope to foster progress in the machine translation community and beyond.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: To avoid bias coming from the document structure, we carefully selected one paragraph per document, from either the beginning, middle or end of the article. We balanced the location selection to be equally distributed across the whole corpus... While translationese (or overly literal or awkward translations) has known idiosyncrasies, we conjecture that these effects are rather marginal...

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: By translating the same set of English sentences in more than hundred languages, we enable evaluation of multilingual MT with the only caveat that source sentences not in English are produced by human translators. While translationese (or overly literal or awkward translations) has known idiosyncrasies (Zhang and Toral, 2019), we conjecture that these effects are rather marginal...

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The dev set is meant to be used for hyper-parameter tuning. The devtest is meant to be used for testing purpose during the development phase... Beyond translation, FLORES-101 can be used to evaluate tasks such as sentence and document classification, language identification, and multilingual domain adaptation.
